en: tycoon; magnate; important figure; big shot; bigwig

examples.en: He is known as a heavyweight in the political world.

examples.ko: 업계 거물이 우리 회사에 투자하기로 했어요.
examples.en: A big name in the industry decided to invest in our company.

examples.ko: 이번 모임에는 재계 거물들이 많이 와요.
examples.en: Many business tycoons are coming to this gathering.

examples.ko: 그는 거물에게도 할 말은 하는 사람이에요.
examples.en: He is someone who speaks his mind even to big shots.

examples.ko: 저는 거물급 인사를 만날 기회가 거의 없어요.
examples.en: I hardly ever get a chance to meet top-level figures.

examples.ko: 작은 가게로 시작해서 지금은 거물이 됐어요.
examples.en: He started with a small shop and has now become a magnate.

explain: 정치, 재계, 연예계처럼 한 분야에서 영향력이 큰 사람을 말해요. '거물급'이나 '거물 정치인'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 자주 써요. 돈을 많이 쓰는 손님은 '큰손'이라고도 하지만, '거물'은 영향력이 큰 사람에게 써요.
explain_en: It refers to someone with great influence in a field such as politics, business, or entertainment. It is often extended as '거물급' or '거물 정치인'. A big spender may be called '큰손', but '거물' is for people with great influence.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 전쟁 때 고향을 떠난 실향민이에요.
examples.en: My grandfather is a displaced person who left his hometown during the war.

examples.ko: 명절이 되면 실향민들은 고향 생각이 더 간절해져요.
examples.en: On holidays, displaced people long for their hometowns even more.
Many displaced people live in this village.

examples.ko: 실향민 가족이 이산가족 상봉 소식을 기다리고 있어요.
examples.en: A displaced family is waiting for news of a family reunion.
I heard the stories of elderly displaced people on the news.

examples.ko: 실향민에게 고향은 가고 싶어도 갈 수 없는 곳이에요.
examples.en: For a displaced person, hometown is a place they cannot go back to even if they want to.

explain: 한국에서는 주로 전쟁과 분단 때문에 북쪽에 있는 고향을 떠나온 사람을 가리킬 때가 많아요. 재해로 집을 잃은 사람은 '이재민', 나라 밖으로 피한 사람은 '난민'이라고 해서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: In Korea it is often used for people who left their hometowns in the North because of the war and division. It differs from '이재민' (people who lost their homes in a disaster) and '난민' (refugees who fled abroad).

examples.ko: 이 길은 사고가 많아서 악명이 높아요.
examples.en: This road has a bad reputation because of many accidents.

examples.ko: 악명 높은 교통 체증에 한 시간 갇혀 있었어요.
examples.en: I was stuck for an hour in the notorious traffic jam.
That restaurant became notorious for its unfriendliness.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 야근이 많다는 악명 때문에 지원자가 줄었어요.
examples.en: Because of the company's reputation for long overtime, applicants decreased.
Despite his bad reputation, he was actually a kind person.
It was a notoriously dangerous mountain road, so I drove carefully.

explain: 나쁜 일로 유명하다는 말이에요. '악명이 높다', '악명이 자자하다'처럼 써요. '유명하다'는 좋은 뜻과 나쁜 뜻 모두 가능하지만 악명은 반드시 나쁜 쪽이에요. 좋은 일로 유명한 것은 '명성'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means being famous for something bad. It is used as '악명이 높다' or '악명이 자자하다'. '유명하다' can be good or bad, but 악명 is always negative. Being famous for good things is called '명성'.

examples.en: A story about the two actors' romance appeared in the news.

examples.ko: 그 정치인은 젊은 시절 염문을 뿌렸다고 해요.
examples.en: They say that politician was rumored to have many romances in his youth.
The singer caught up in a romance rumor held a press conference.
The two strongly denied the rumors of a romance.
The romance rumor spread quickly.

examples.ko: 그 영화감독은 염문 때문에 한동안 일을 못 했어요.
examples.en: That film director couldn't work for a while because of a romance scandal.

explain: 외래어 '스캔들'과 달리 연애나 사랑에 관한 소문에만 써요. 주로 연예인이나 유명인 기사에서 보는 글말이고, 일상 대화에서는 '연애설'이라고 많이 해요.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 젊을 때 여러 사람과 염문을 뿌렸어요.
phrases.en: That actor was linked romantically with many people when he was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번이 아니라 여러 사람과 연애 소문이 난다는 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스나 이야기에서 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It suggests romance rumors with several people, not just once. It is used in news and storytelling.
phrases.en_equiv: be rumored to have many romances

explain_en: Unlike the loanword '스캔들', it is used only for rumors about romance. It is mostly written language seen in articles about celebrities, and in conversation people often say '연애설'.

examples.en: An influential person in that area sponsored the event.
I started the business without help from anyone powerful.
The influential people of the village gathered and held a meeting.
There is a rumor that he is close to a powerful figure in politics.
If I ask a powerful person, will things work out quickly?

examples.ko: 유력자라고 해서 법을 어겨도 되는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being influential doesn't mean you can break the law.

explain: 정치, 경제, 지역 사회에서 영향력이 큰 사람을 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '실력자'가 있고, 연줄이나 힘을 가진 사람이라는 느낌이 있어서 문맥에 따라 약간 부정적으로 들리기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a person with great influence in politics, business or a local community. A similar word is '실력자', and it suggests someone with connections and power, so depending on context it can sound slightly negative.

examples.en: The police finally caught the real culprit.
Evidence came out that the real culprit is someone else.
In the final episode, the real culprit was an unexpected person.

examples.ko: 처음에 잡힌 사람은 진범과 아무 관계가 없었어요.
examples.en: The person first caught had nothing to do with the real culprit.

examples.ko: 모두가 그를 진범으로 믿었지만 사실은 아니었어요.
examples.en: Everyone believed he was the real culprit, but he wasn't.

examples.ko: 누가 진범인지 끝까지 알 수 없었어요.
examples.en: We couldn't tell who the real culprit was until the end.

explain: 다른 사람이 억울하게 의심받을 때 '진짜 범인'을 가리키는 말이에요. '진범을 잡다/밝히다', '진범이 따로 있다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It points to the true criminal, especially when someone else has been wrongly suspected. It is often used as '진범을 잡다/밝히다' and '진범이 따로 있다'.

examples.en: He was a revolutionary who tried to change the country.

examples.ko: 그 혁명가는 평생 자유를 위해 싸웠어요.
examples.en: That revolutionary fought for freedom all his life.
The revolutionaries gathered in secret and made a plan.
I watched a movie about the life of a revolutionary.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 꿈은 혁명가가 되는 거였어요.
examples.en: My childhood dream was to become a revolutionary.
For the young revolutionary, time was always short.

explain: 사회나 정치 체제를 크게 뒤집으려고 앞장서는 사람을 가리켜요. '운동가'는 사회운동을 하는 사람을 넓게 가리키는 말이라, 혁명가는 그보다 체제를 바꾸려는 뜻이 훨씬 강해요. 역사 이야기나 영화, 책에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who takes the lead in overturning a social or political system. '운동가' (activist) covers anyone in social movements, so 혁명가 carries a much stronger sense of changing the system itself. It often appears in history, films and books.
